name: red slope 3x4
where: the red 3x4 slope brick, sloped face up, against the left edge of the plate, with several rows of empty plate above it and below it
checks: the brick touches the left edge of the plate
it is red
there are empty studs both above it and below it (it touches neither the top nor the bottom edge of the plate)

name: purple 2x4 cab
where: the purple 2x4 brick lying flat with its long side running front to back (2 studs wide, 4 studs deep), directly to the right of the red slope and touching it; its bottom is level with the red brick's bottom and it reaches one stud further up than the red brick
checks: the purple brick touches the right side of the red slope
its long side runs front to back (it is deeper than it is wide), not left to right
it reaches one stud further up than the red brick

name: green 1x2 exhaust
where: the small lime-green 1x2 brick lying flat with its long side running front to back (1 wide, 2 deep), immediately to the right of the purple brick at its upper corner, reaching one stud further up than the purple brick like an exhaust pipe
checks: the lime brick touches the right side of the purple brick
its long side runs front to back, not left to right
it reaches one stud further up than the purple brick

name: white 1x6 top
where: the first white 1x6 brick lying flat, directly to the right of the purple brick with its left end touching the purple brick, just under the lime exhaust (the exhaust sits on top of its left end)
checks: the brick is pure white, not beige or cream
it is horizontal, 6 studs long
its left end touches the purple brick

name: white 1x6 middle
where: the second white 1x6 brick lying flat directly below the first white brick, same length, left end touching the purple brick, ends lined up with the brick above; together the two white bricks form one white block two studs deep
checks: the white area to the right of the purple brick is two studs deep (two 1x6 bricks side by side), not one
its left end touches the purple brick
its right end lines up with the right end of the brick above

name: blue 1x4 lower-left
where: the blue 1x4 brick lying flat directly under the lower white brick, its left end touching the purple brick, its right end stopping two studs short of the white bricks' right end; its bottom is level with the bottom of the red and purple bricks
checks: the blue brick's left end touches the purple brick
it sits directly under the lower white brick with no gap
its right end is two studs short of the white bricks' right end

name: green 1x2 lower-right
where: the lime-green 1x2 brick lying flat to the right of the blue brick and touching it, filling the row so that its right end lines up with the white bricks' right end
checks: the lime brick touches the right end of the blue brick
it is horizontal, in the same row as the blue brick
its right end lines up with the right end of the white bricks above

name: white 1x4 at the right end of the body, long side front to back
where: the white 1x4 brick lying flat with its long side running front to back (1 wide, 4 deep) against the right end of the body, touching the ends of the two white bricks and the lime brick; it reaches one stud further up than the top white brick and its bottom is level with the body's bottom
checks: its long side runs front to back (it is deeper than it is wide), not left to right
it touches the right ends of the white bricks and the lime brick
it reaches one stud further up than the top white brick

name: red disc front wheel
where: the red round disc (4 studs across) directly under the red slope, touching its bottom edge, same width as the slope, against the left edge of the plate, like a front wheel
checks: the disc touches the bottom edge of the red slope
it is as wide as the red slope and lined up with it
it touches the left edge of the plate

name: red disc rear wheel
where: the second red round disc under the right part of the body as the rear wheel: its top touches the blue and lime bricks, its right edge stays left of the lime brick's right end, and bare green plate shows directly below the white 1x4 at the right end of the body
checks: the disc's top touches the bottom of the body (the blue and lime bricks)
directly below the white 1x4 at the right end of the body there is bare green plate, not the disc
the disc's right edge is to the left of the lime brick's right end

name: tan 1x6 ground left
where: the tan (beige) 1x6 brick lying flat directly under the front disc, its left end at the left edge of the plate, like the ground line
checks: the brick is beige/tan, not white
it is horizontal and lies directly under the front disc
its left end is at the left edge of the plate

name: white 1x6 ground mid
where: the white 1x6 brick lying flat in the same row as the tan brick, continuing it to the right and touching it, running under the rear disc
checks: the brick is pure white
it is in the same row as the tan brick and touches its right end
it runs under the rear disc

name: yellow 1x4 ground right
where: the yellow 1x4 brick lying flat in the same row, continuing the white ground brick to the right and touching it, filling the row to the last stud column of the plate below the white 1x4 at the right end of the body
checks: the brick is yellow
it is in the same row as the white ground brick and touches its right end
its right end is at the right edge of the plate: no empty studs to its right in that row (the brick may look flush with or slightly past the plate's edge)
